title: P50-family MTP weight schedule: DeepSeek-V3's lambda 0.3 -> 0.1 drop for the last third of pretraining (0.3 until 67.6% of the 300 s wall-clock, then 0.1), on the 136-fable MTP Lean incumbent (4,800,000 params)
description: Idea ID: P50-family (the 136-fable multi-token-prediction objective; nearest backlog entry P50): the pretraining-only MTP loss weight follows DeepSeek-V3's (2024) published schedule, 0.3 for the first 10/14.8 = 67.6% of the pretraining wall-clock and 0.1 for the rest, instead of 136's constant 0.3; nothing else changes and the handoff architecture is identical (4,800,000 params). It should help expert iteration because the MTP gain looks front-loaded (it shapes planning features while the LR is high), while the handoff weights are set in the last third, where a trunk refocused on the next-token distribution the RL sampler actually draws from should give a slightly better calibrated, higher-sample-accuracy start; 142-fable (P50 deep supervision, running now) is a different auxiliary loss and is not duplicated.
hypothesis: 136-fable's MTP (+11.7 vs 129 at constant weight 0.3) is not monotone in auxiliary pressure: 138-fable (a second shared t+3 stage, total aux 0.6) lost 17 and 141-claude (a harder parallel t+2 target) lost 21. Pretraining is data-limited (main val loss flat from ~90 s while train loss keeps falling), so the MTP signal's useful work is early representation shaping, and in the last third (lr 0.49 -> 0.30 of peak, the phase that sets the handoff state) a 0.3-weighted t+2 loss mostly competes with the next-token loss for trunk capacity. Dropping it to 0.1 there, as DeepSeek-V3 does for the tail of pretraining, keeps a weak planning signal while letting the trunk end on the objective the sampler uses, which should raise round-1 sample accuracy/targets solved and end above 658. Mechanism checks: steps unchanged vs 136 (same compute per step); main train loss over the last third equal to or slightly below 136's (~0.055); main val loss 0.076-0.090; the (unweighted) mtp_loss rises a little after the switch relative to 136's ~0.055; held-out greedy 0.955-0.975. Failure modes: (a) the late MTP signal is the part that helps (it regularizes the overfitting phase), so weakening it lets the trunk memorize more and transfer worse, a loss of 10-30; (b) no measurable effect, 0 plus noise (sd of a 3-seed mean difference ~20-25).
expected_delta: -35 to +30 theorems at >=7 vs 658 (central guess +3); pretraining 3,330-3,420 steps (136: 3,351-3,370), final main val loss 0.076-0.090, held-out greedy 0.955-0.975, round-1 targets solved within +-120 of 136's per seed, total secs 1,450-1,750 (sampling cost unchanged), no added timeout risk

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, unchanged from 136-fable (forward() calls features(), which returns (final hidden state, ALiBi bias) for the pretraining-only MTP module)
arch.change: none vs 136-fable: same 6 Peri-LN blocks, 4,800,000 params, same forward function, same pretraining-only MTPHead (never registered on the model, dropped when pretrain() returns). Only the weight on the MTP loss changes over the wall-clock (see loss.total)
arch.n_params_detail: model: identical to 136-fable, 4,800,000 (vocab 107; CPU check model.n_params() == 4,800,000). MTP module (pretraining only, not on the model): 922,880, unchanged from 136
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks, then load state: same keys and same function as 136-fable/129-claude. The MTP module is not saved

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial); the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (256,512) input proj) join the Muon group and its LayerNorm gains/biases and projection biases join AdamW, same lr, schedule and decay as the trunk
optimizer.schedule: unchanged from 129/136: cosine over wall-clock, after the 200-step linear warmup lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: unchanged from 129/136: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 129's 24 hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (256,512; RMS shape scale sqrt(2)): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are unchanged

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: CHANGED: main + w(frac) * mtp, w = MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 while frac = elapsed / budget < MTP_SWITCH = 10/14.8 = 0.6757 (~203 s of 300 s), then MTP_WEIGHT_LATE = 0.1 for the rest; a step change, no ramp. This is DeepSeek-V3's (2024) published schedule (lambda 0.3 for the first 10T tokens, 0.1 for the remaining 4.8T) mapped onto the wall-clock fraction; 136-fable used 0.3 constant. At the switch the AdamW/Muon lr factor is 0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(0.6757 pi)) = 0.49 of peak. curve points still record the mean recent (unweighted) mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]
loss.schedule_check: CPU check: mtp_loss(model, mtp, x, m, w) returns main + w * aux exactly (abs diff 0.0) for w = 0.3 and 0.1; the weight is chosen per step from the same frac that drives the lr schedule
